To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the environment can modulate the expression of genes and their epigenetic regulation.
the environmental risk factors for ASD can modulate gene expression and the epigenome of susceptible individuals.
environmental risk factors can modulate the epigenome and genome of individuals susceptible to autism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of mechanisms through which environmental factors can modulate the epigenome and genome of susceptible individuals.
identifying and understanding the molecular and genetic mechanisms by which environmental risk factors increase the incidence of autism.
identifying and characterizing gene-environment interactions in ASD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genome and epignome of individuals susceptible to ASD are highly modifiable by environmental risk factors.

environmental factors, such as maternal stress and infection during pregnancy, can alter the genome and/or epigenome and thus the phenotype of genetically susceptible individuals, leading to the development of ASD.
environmental risk factors can alter the genome and epigeome in susceptible individuals in many different ways, which can be either direct or indirect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genome and epignome are modulated by environmental factors in susceptible individuals.
environmental factors may modulate the genome or epigenome of susceptible individuals through a variety of mechanisms.

environmental exposures can affect the genome and epignome of genetically-suspceptible individuals through a variety of mechanisms including: (1) direct effects on gene expression, (2) indirect effects on gene expression via modulation of the epigenome, (3) direct and indirect effects on gene regulation through epigenetic processes, and (4) direct and indirect interactions with DNA and chromatin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modulation of gene expression and epigenome by environmental risk factors can be a result of a variety of different molecular mechanisms and pathways.
environmental factors implicated with ASD can alter the genome and epigeome in a variety of ways.
there are many ways through which environmental factors can interact with genes to cause ASD.
